question.prompt: A teacher gave a test to a class in which \(10\%\) of the students are juniors and \(90\%\) are seniors. The average score on the test was \(84.\) The juniors all received the same score, and the average score of the seniors was \(83.\) What score did each of the juniors receive on the test?

solutions.explanation:
The percentages show that there are nine seniors for every junior. This ratio tells us how much each group's average contributes to the class total.

Let \(n>0\) be the number of juniors, and let \(j\) be their common score. There are \(9n\) seniors and \(10n\) students altogether. Since total score equals average score times number of students,
\[
nj+9n\cdot83=10n\cdot84.
\]
Divide by the positive number \(n\) and solve:
\[
j=10\cdot84-9\cdot83=840-747=93.
\]
Each junior received \(93\), choice C.
solutions.title: Use the two groups' score totals

solutions.explanation:
Compare every score with the class average of \(84\). The total amount below \(84\) must equal the total amount above it, because replacing every score by \(84\) would leave the class total unchanged.

The seniors average \(83\), so their total is short by one point per senior. There are nine seniors for every junior, making this a shortage of nine points per junior. Since all juniors have the same score, each must contribute nine points above \(84\) to balance that shortage.
\[
84+9=93.
\]
Thus each junior received \(93\), choice C.
solutions.title: Balance the differences from 84
